Definition: from a derivative of G1492; to be knowing (learned), i.e. (by implication) to visit for information (interview):--see.
BiblicalUsage: In Scripture, historéō means to visit, to get to know. It occurs just once, in Galatians.
TheologicalSignificance: I read historéō plainly: to visit, to get to know, and I leave it there.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
